audit_status.source_base: Hebrew Numbers / Bemidbar Miriam, Meribah, Edom, and Aaron-death text tradition, draft aligned later
audit_status.review_note: First-pass draft reviewed for Miriam's death, no-water crisis, speaking/striking the rock, Moses and Aaron's exclusion, Edom's refusal of passage, route change, transfer of priestly garments, Aaron's death, and communal mourning. Strong grief, anti-authoritarian, territorial-sovereignty, and anti-victim-blaming safeguards required.

verses.restored: Children of Israel, all congregation, came to wilderness of Zin in first month, and people stayed at Kadesh. Miriam died there and was buried there.

familiar.text: Then came the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, into the desert of Zin in the first month: and the people abode in Kadesh; and Miriam died there, and was buried there.

modern.text: In the first month, the whole congregation of Israel entered the Wilderness of Zin and stayed in Kadesh. There Miriam died and was buried.

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֣אוּ בְנֵֽי יִ֠שְׂרָאֵל כָּל הָ֨עֵדָ֤ה מִדְבַּר צִן֙ בַּחֹ֣דֶשׁ הָֽרִאשׁ֔וֹן וַיֵּ֥שֶׁב הָעָ֖ם בְּקָדֵ֑שׁ וַתָּ֤מָת שָׁם֙ מִרְיָ֔ם וַתִּקָּבֵ֖ר שָֽׁם

verses.restored: There was no water for congregation, and they assembled against Moses and Aaron.

familiar.text: And there was no water for the congregation: and they gathered themselves together against Moses and against Aaron.

modern.text: Now there was no water for the congregation, so they gathered against Moses and Aaron.

original.text: וְלֹא הָ֥יָה מַ֖יִם לָעֵדָ֑ה וַיִּקָּ֣הֲל֔וּ עַל מֹשֶׁ֖ה וְעַֽל אַהֲרֹֽן

verses.restored: The people contended with Moses and said, Would that we had perished when our brothers perished before YHWH!

familiar.text: And the people chode with Moses, and spake, saying, Would God that we had died when our brethren died before the LORD!

modern.text: The people quarreled with Moses and said, “If only we had perished with our brothers before the LORD!

original.text: וַיָּ֥רֶב הָעָ֖ם עִם מֹשֶׁ֑ה וַיֹּאמְר֣וּ לֵאמֹ֔ר וְל֥וּ גָוַ֛עְנוּ בִּגְוַ֥ע אַחֵ֖ינוּ לִפְנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: Why have you brought assembly of YHWH into this wilderness, for us and our livestock to die there?

familiar.text: And why have ye brought up the congregation of the LORD into this wilderness, that we and our cattle should die there?

modern.text: Why have you brought the LORD’s assembly into this wilderness for us and our livestock to die here?

original.text: וְלָמָ֤ה הֲבֵאתֶם֙ אֶת קְהַ֣ל יְהוָ֔ה אֶל הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר הַזֶּ֑ה לָמ֣וּת שָׁ֔ם אֲנַ֖חְנוּ וּבְעִירֵֽנוּ

verses.restored: Why did you bring us up from Egypt to bring us to this evil place? It is no place of seed, fig, vine, or pomegranate, and there is no water to drink.

familiar.text: And wherefore have ye made us to come up out of Egypt, to bring us in unto this evil place? it is no place of seed, or of figs, or of vines, or of pomegranates; neither is there any water to drink.

modern.text: Why have you led us up out of Egypt to bring us to this wretched place? It is not a place of grain, figs, vines, or pomegranates—and there is no water to drink!”

original.text: וְלָמָ֤ה הֶֽעֱלִיתֻ֨נוּ֙ מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם לְהָבִ֣יא אֹתָ֔נוּ אֶל הַמָּק֥וֹם הָרָ֖ע הַזֶּ֑ה לֹ֣א מְק֣וֹם זֶ֗רַע וּתְאֵנָ֤ה וְגֶ֨פֶן֙ וְרִמּ֔וֹן וּמַ֥יִם אַ֖יִן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron went from face of assembly to entrance of tent of meeting and fell upon their faces, and glory of YHWH appeared to them.

familiar.text: And Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly unto the door of the tabernacle of the congregation, and they fell upon their faces: and the glory of the LORD appeared unto them.

modern.text: Then Moses and Aaron went from the presence of the assembly to the entrance to the Tent of Meeting. They fell facedown, and the glory of the LORD appeared to them.

original.text: וַיָּבֹא֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה וְאַהֲרֹ֜ן מִפְּנֵ֣י הַקָּהָ֗ל אֶל פֶּ֨תַח֙ אֹ֣הֶל מוֹעֵ֔ד וַֽיִּפְּל֖וּ עַל פְּנֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּרָ֥א כְבוֹד יְהוָ֖ה אֲלֵיהֶֽם

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses, saying,

modern.text: And the LORD said to Moses,

original.text: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Take staff and assemble congregation, you and Aaron your brother, and speak to rock before their eyes, and it shall give its water. You shall bring out water for them from rock and give drink to congregation and their livestock.

familiar.text: Take the rod, and gather thou the assembly together, thou, and Aaron thy brother, and speak ye unto the rock before their eyes; and it shall give forth his water, and thou shalt bring forth to them water out of the rock: so thou shalt give the congregation and their beasts drink.

modern.text: “Take the staff and assemble the congregation. You and your brother Aaron are to speak to the rock while they watch, and it will pour out its water. You will bring out water from the rock and provide drink for the congregation and their livestock.”

original.text: קַ֣ח אֶת הַמַּטֶּ֗ה וְהַקְהֵ֤ל אֶת הָעֵדָה֙ אַתָּה֙ וְאַהֲרֹ֣ן אָחִ֔יךָ וְדִבַּרְתֶּ֧ם אֶל הַסֶּ֛לַע לְעֵינֵיהֶ֖ם וְנָתַ֣ן מֵימָ֑יו וְהוֹצֵאתָ֨ לָהֶ֥ם מַ֨יִם֙ מִן הַסֶּ֔לַע וְהִשְׁקִיתָ֥ אֶת הָעֵדָ֖ה וְאֶת בְּעִירָֽם

verses.restored: Moses took staff from before YHWH as he commanded him.

familiar.text: And Moses took the rod from before the LORD, as he commanded him.

modern.text: So Moses took the staff from the LORD’s presence, just as he had been commanded.

original.text: וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת הַמַּטֶּ֖ה מִלִּפְנֵ֣י יְהוָ֑ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּֽהוּ

verses.restored: Moses and Aaron assembled assembly before rock, and he said to them, Hear, please, rebels! From this rock shall we bring out water for you?

familiar.text: And Moses and Aaron gathered the congregation together before the rock, and he said unto them, Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?

modern.text: Then Moses and Aaron gathered the assembly in front of the rock, and Moses said to them, “Listen now, you rebels, must we bring you water out of this rock?”

original.text: וַיַּקְהִ֜לוּ מֹשֶׁ֧ה וְאַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת הַקָּהָ֖ל אֶל פְּנֵ֣י הַסָּ֑לַע וַיֹּ֣אמֶר לָהֶ֗ם שִׁמְעוּ נָא֙ הַמֹּרִ֔ים הֲמִן הַסֶּ֣לַע הַזֶּ֔ה נוֹצִ֥יא לָכֶ֖ם מָֽיִם

verses.restored: Moses lifted his hand and struck rock with his staff twice; abundant water came out, and congregation and their livestock drank.

familiar.text: And Moses lifted up his hand, and with his rod he smote the rock twice: and the water came out abundantly, and the congregation drank, and their beasts also.

modern.text: Then Moses raised his hand and struck the rock twice with his staff, so that a great amount of water gushed out, and the congregation and their livestock were able to drink.

original.text: וַיָּ֨רֶם מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶת יָד֗וֹ וַיַּ֧ךְ אֶת הַסֶּ֛לַע בְּמַטֵּ֖הוּ פַּעֲמָ֑יִם וַיֵּצְאוּ֙ מַ֣יִם רַבִּ֔ים וַתֵּ֥שְׁתְּ הָעֵדָ֖ה וּבְעִירָֽם

verses.restored: YHWH said to Moses and Aaron, Because you did not trust me to sanctify me before eyes of children of Israel, therefore you shall not bring this assembly into land that I have given them.

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron, Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel, therefore ye shall not bring this congregation into the land which I have given them.

modern.text: But the LORD said to Moses and Aaron, “Because you did not trust Me to show My holiness in the sight of the Israelites, you will not bring this assembly into the land that I have given them.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָה֮ אֶל מֹשֶׁ֣ה וְאֶֽל אַהֲרֹן֒ יַ֚עַן לֹא הֶאֱמַנְתֶּ֣ם בִּ֔י לְהַ֨קְדִּישֵׁ֔נִי לְעֵינֵ֖י בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לָכֵ֗ן לֹ֤א תָבִ֨יאוּ֙ אֶת הַקָּהָ֣ל הַזֶּ֔ה אֶל הָאָ֖רֶץ אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי לָהֶֽם

verses.restored: These are waters of Meribah/Contention, where children of Israel contended with YHWH, and he was sanctified among them.

familiar.text: This is the water of Meribah; because the children of Israel strove with the LORD, and he was sanctified in them.

modern.text: These were the waters of Meribah, where the Israelites quarreled with the LORD, and He showed His holiness among them. Edom Refuses Passage

original.text: הֵ֚מָּה מֵ֣י מְרִיבָ֔ה אֲשֶׁר רָב֥וּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל אֶת יְהוָ֑ה וַיִּקָּדֵ֖שׁ בָּֽם

verses.restored: Moses sent messengers from Kadesh to king of Edom: Thus says your brother Israel: You know all hardship that found us.

familiar.text: And Moses sent messengers from Kadesh unto the king of Edom, Thus saith thy brother Israel, Thou knowest all the travail that hath befallen us:

modern.text: From Kadesh, Moses sent messengers to tell the king of Edom, “This is what your brother Israel says: You know all the hardship that has befallen us,

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח מֹשֶׁ֧ה מַלְאָכִ֛ים מִקָּדֵ֖שׁ אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ אֱד֑וֹם כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ אָחִ֣יךָ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֥ת כָּל הַתְּלָאָ֖ה אֲשֶׁ֥ר מְצָאָֽתְנוּ

verses.restored: Our fathers went down to Egypt, and we dwelt in Egypt many days; Egyptians did evil to us and our fathers.

familiar.text: How our fathers went down into Egypt, and we have dwelt in Egypt a long time; and the Egyptians vexed us, and our fathers:

modern.text: how our fathers went down to Egypt, where we lived many years. The Egyptians mistreated us and our fathers,

original.text: וַיֵּרְד֤וּ אֲבֹתֵ֨ינוּ֙ מִצְרַ֔יְמָה וַנֵּ֥שֶׁב בְּמִצְרַ֖יִם יָמִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וַיָּרֵ֥עוּ לָ֛נוּ מִצְרַ֖יִם וְלַאֲבֹתֵֽינוּ

verses.restored: We cried to YHWH, and he heard our voice and sent a messenger and brought us out from Egypt. And look, we are at Kadesh, a city at edge of your border.

familiar.text: And when we cried unto the LORD, he heard our voice, and sent an angel, and hath brought us forth out of Egypt: and, behold, we are in Kadesh, a city in the uttermost of thy border:

modern.text: and when we cried out to the LORD, He heard our voice, sent an angel, and brought us out of Egypt. Now look, we are in Kadesh, a city on the edge of your territory.

original.text: וַנִּצְעַ֤ק אֶל יְהוָה֙ וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע קֹלֵ֔נוּ וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח מַלְאָ֔ךְ וַיֹּצִאֵ֖נוּ מִמִּצְרָ֑יִם וְהִנֵּה֙ אֲנַ֣חְנוּ בְקָדֵ֔שׁ עִ֖יר קְצֵ֥ה גְבוּלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Please let us pass through your land. We will not pass through field or vineyard, and we will not drink water of a well; by king's road we will go, not turning right or left until we pass through your border.

familiar.text: Let us pass, I pray thee, through thy country: we will not pass through the fields, or through the vineyards, neither will we drink of the water of the wells: we will go by the king’s high way, we will not turn to the right hand nor to the left, until we have passed thy borders.

modern.text: Please let us pass through your land. We will not cut through any field or vineyard, or drink water from any well. We will stay on the King’s Highway; we will not turn to the right or to the left until we have passed through your territory.”

original.text: נַעְבְּרָה נָּ֣א בְאַרְצֶ֗ךָ לֹ֤א נַעֲבֹר֙ בְּשָׂדֶ֣ה וּבְכֶ֔רֶם וְלֹ֥א נִשְׁתֶּ֖ה מֵ֣י בְאֵ֑ר דֶּ֧רֶךְ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ נֵלֵ֗ךְ לֹ֤א נִטֶּה֙ יָמִ֣ין וּשְׂמֹ֔אול עַ֥ד אֲשֶֽׁר נַעֲבֹ֖ר גְּבוּלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Edom said to him, You shall not pass through me, lest I come out with sword to meet you.

familiar.text: And Edom said unto him, Thou shalt not pass by me, lest I come out against thee with the sword.

modern.text: But Edom answered, “You may not travel through our land, or we will come out and confront you with the sword.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ אֱד֔וֹם לֹ֥א תַעֲבֹ֖ר בִּ֑י פֶּן בַּחֶ֖רֶב אֵצֵ֥א לִקְרָאתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Children of Israel said to him, By highway we will go up, and if we drink your water, I and my livestock, I will give its price; only let me pass through on my feet, nothing more.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel said unto him, We will go by the high way: and if I and my cattle drink of thy water, then I will pay for it: I will only, without doing anything else, go through on my feet.

modern.text: “We will stay on the main road,” the Israelites replied, “and if we or our herds drink your water, we will pay for it. There will be no problem; only let us pass through on foot.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמְר֨וּ אֵלָ֥יו בְּנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֘ל בַּֽמְסִלָּ֣ה נַעֲלֶה֒ וְאִם מֵימֶ֤יךָ נִשְׁתֶּה֙ אֲנִ֣י וּמִקְנַ֔י וְנָתַתִּ֖י מִכְרָ֑ם רַ֥ק אֵין דָּבָ֖ר בְּרַגְלַ֥י אֶֽעֱבֹֽרָה

verses.restored: He said, You shall not pass. Edom came out to meet him with heavy people and strong hand.

familiar.text: And he said, Thou shalt not go through. And Edom came out against him with much people, and with a strong hand.

modern.text: But Edom insisted, “You may not pass through.” And they came out to confront the Israelites with a large army and a strong hand.

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לֹ֣א תַעֲבֹ֑ר וַיֵּצֵ֤א אֱדוֹם֙ לִקְרָאת֔וֹ בְּעַ֥ם כָּבֵ֖ד וּבְיָ֥ד חֲזָקָֽה

verses.restored: Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through his territory, and Israel turned away from him.

familiar.text: Thus Edom refused to give Israel passage through his border: wherefore Israel turned away from him.

modern.text: So Edom refused to allow Israel to pass through their territory, and Israel turned away from them. The Death of Aaron

original.text: וַיְמָאֵ֣ן אֱד֗וֹם נְתֹן֙ אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל עֲבֹ֖ר בִּגְבֻל֑וֹ וַיֵּ֥ט יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵעָלָֽיו

verses.restored: They set out from Kadesh, and children of Israel, all congregation, came to Mount Hor.

familiar.text: And the children of Israel, even the whole congregation, journeyed from Kadesh, and came unto mount Hor.

modern.text: After they had set out from Kadesh, the whole congregation of Israel came to Mount Hor.

original.text: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִקָּדֵ֑שׁ וַיָּבֹ֧אוּ בְנֵֽי יִשְׂרָאֵ֛ל כָּל הָעֵדָ֖ה הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר

verses.restored: YHWH spoke to Moses and Aaron at Mount Hor, by border of land of Edom, saying,

familiar.text: And the LORD spake unto Moses and Aaron in mount Hor, by the coast of the land of Edom, saying,

modern.text: And at Mount Hor, near the border of the land of Edom, the LORD said to Moses and Aaron,

original.text: וַיֹּ֧אמֶר יְהוָ֛ה אֶל מֹשֶׁ֥ה וְאֶֽל אַהֲרֹ֖ן בְּהֹ֣ר הָהָ֑ר עַל גְּב֥וּל אֶֽרֶץ אֱד֖וֹם לֵאמֹֽר

verses.restored: Aaron shall be gathered to his people, for he shall not enter land I have given to children of Israel, because you rebelled against my mouth/command at waters of Meribah.

familiar.text: Aaron shall be gathered unto his people: for he shall not enter into the land which I have given unto the children of Israel, because ye rebelled against my word at the water of Meribah.

modern.text: “Aaron will be gathered to his people; he will not enter the land that I have given the Israelites, because both of you rebelled against My command at the waters of Meribah.

original.text: יֵאָסֵ֤ף אַהֲרֹן֙ אֶל עַמָּ֔יו כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָבֹא֙ אֶל הָאָ֔רֶץ אֲשֶׁ֥ר נָתַ֖תִּי לִבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עַ֛ל אֲשֶׁר מְרִיתֶ֥ם אֶת פִּ֖י לְמֵ֥י מְרִיבָֽה

modern.text: Take Aaron and his son Eleazar and bring them up Mount Hor.

original.text: קַ֚ח אֶֽת אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאֶת אֶלְעָזָ֖ר בְּנ֑וֹ וְהַ֥עַל אֹתָ֖ם הֹ֥ר הָהָֽר

modern.text: Remove Aaron’s priestly garments and put them on his son Eleazar. Aaron will be gathered to his people and will die there.”

modern.text: So Moses did as the LORD had commanded, and they climbed Mount Hor in the sight of the whole congregation.

original.text: וַיַּ֣עַשׂ מֹשֶׁ֔ה כַּאֲשֶׁ֖ר צִוָּ֣ה יְהוָ֑ה וַֽיַּעֲלוּ֙ אֶל הֹ֣ר הָהָ֔ר לְעֵינֵ֖י כָּל הָעֵדָֽה

familiar.text: And Moses stripped Aaron of his garments, and put them upon Eleazar his son; and Aaron died there in the top of the mount: and Moses and Eleazar came down from the mount.

modern.text: After Moses had removed Aaron’s garments and put them on his son Eleazar, Aaron died there on top of the mountain. Then Moses and Eleazar came down from the mountain.

original.text: וַיַּפְשֵׁט֩ מֹשֶׁ֨ה אֶֽת אַהֲרֹ֜ן אֶת בְּגָדָ֗יו וַיַּלְבֵּ֤שׁ אֹתָם֙ אֶת אֶלְעָזָ֣ר בְּנ֔וֹ וַיָּ֧מָת אַהֲרֹ֛ן שָׁ֖ם בְּרֹ֣אשׁ הָהָ֑ר וַיֵּ֧רֶד מֹשֶׁ֛ה וְאֶלְעָזָ֖ר מִן הָהָֽר

verses.restored: All congregation saw that Aaron had died, and all house of Israel wept for Aaron thirty days.

familiar.text: And when all the congregation saw that Aaron was dead, they mourned for Aaron thirty days, even all the house of Israel.

modern.text: When the whole congregation saw that Aaron had died, the entire house of Israel mourned for him thirty days.

original.text: וַיִּרְאוּ֙ כָּל הָ֣עֵדָ֔ה כִּ֥י גָוַ֖ע אַהֲרֹ֑ן וַיִּבְכּ֤וּ אֶֽת אַהֲרֹן֙ שְׁלֹשִׁ֣ים י֔וֹם כֹּ֖ל בֵּ֥ית יִשְׂרָאֵֽל

translation_notes: Miriam's death is stated briefly, yet it opens a chapter dominated by water crisis, leadership strain, and the death of Aaron; grief must remain visible even where the narrative is terse.
The people's demand for water is materially legitimate. Their rhetoric may be accusatory, but thirst is not a moral failure.
YHWH commands Moses to speak to the rock; Moses instead addresses the people as rebels and strikes twice. The text holds leaders accountable even when water is still provided.
Moses and Aaron's exclusion must not be used to claim one mistake erases a person's whole life or service.
Edom has an existing border and refuses passage. Israel turns away rather than forcing entry, an important limit on movement through another people's territory.
Aaron's garments pass to Eleazar before Aaron dies, separating continuity of office from immortality of officeholder.
Thirty days of communal mourning recognize Aaron's death as a shared loss.
safety_note: Do not use Numbers 20 to shame people for needing water, excuse leaders who lash out under pressure, erase Miriam's importance, override another people's territorial refusal, or teach that grief must be brief and tidy. The chapter holds need, failure, boundary, succession, and mourning together.
